{{short description|Turkish-born American mathematician}}
'''Gizem Karaali''' is a Professor of Mathematics at [[Pomona College]] in [[Claremont, California|Claremont, CA]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/gizem-karaali|title=Faculty page for Gizem Karaali, Pomona College|date=June 2015|access-date=March 4, 2019|archive-date=August 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809054750/https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/gizem-karaali|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Background and education==

Mathematician Gizem Karaali is originally from [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]].
Her father was an electrical engineer and her mother was a professor of nutrition science.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ihouse.berkeley.edu/alumni/times/timesS98/prof.html|title=Resident Profile|year=1998|website=International House Berkeley|access-date=18 March 2019|archive-date=27 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327051419/http://ihouse.berkeley.edu/alumni/times/timesS98/prof.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
She graduated from UAA (the [[Üsküdar American Academy]]) and then went on to [[Boğaziçi University]] where she graduated (with honors) in 1997 with undergraduate degrees in electrical engineering and mathematics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://pages.pomona.edu/~gk014747/research/GK-CV.pdf|title=GK-CV|access-date=February 28, 2019|archive-date=March 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301140018/http://pages.pomona.edu/~gk014747/research/GK-CV.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>  Karaali earned her PhD in mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 2004. Her dissertation was "r-Matrices on Lie Superalgebras" and her advisors were [[Nicolai Reshetikhin|Nikolai Jurieviç Reshetikhin]] and [[Vera Serganova|Vera V. Serganova]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=84607|title=Gizem Karaali - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-02-28|archive-date=2018-08-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809165622/https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=84607|url-status=live}}</ref>   After a two-year postdoctoral position at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], she moved on to [[Pomona College]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pages.pomona.edu/~gk014747/research/GK-CV.pdf|title=GK-CV|access-date=February 28, 2019|archive-date=March 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301140018/http://pages.pomona.edu/~gk014747/research/GK-CV.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==

Karaali's services to the scholarly and mathematical communities include editorship positions for three journals.  She is the  co-editor, along with Mark Huber, of the ''[[Journal of Humanistic Mathematics]]''—an online, open-access journal that focuses on the connections of mathematics to disciplines in the humanities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/gizem-karaali#!tabset_0=1|title=EXPERTISE - Faculty page for Gizem Karaali, Pomona College|date=June 2015|access-date=March 4, 2019|archive-date=August 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809054750/https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/gizem-karaali#!tabset_0=1|url-status=live}}</ref>  She is an Associate Editor<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/mathematics/journal/283?detailsPage=editorialBoard|title=Mathematical Intelligencer Editorial Board|access-date=March 4, 2019|archive-date=November 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120053611/https://www.springer.com/mathematics/journal/283?detailsPage=editorialBoard|url-status=live}}</ref> for ''[[The Mathematical Intelligencer]]'', a journal that offers—to mathematicians and those outside the field—articles about mathematics and mathematicians and about the history and culture of mathematics. She also is an Associate Editor<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholarcommons.usf.edu/numeracy/editorialboard.html|title=Numeracy Editorial Board|access-date=March 4, 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811085521/http://scholarcommons.usf.edu/numeracy/editorialboard.html|url-status=live}}</ref> for ''Numeracy''—the open-access, peer-reviewed journal of the [[National Numeracy Network]] (NNN).  Her Faculty page at Pomona College <ref name=":0" /> offers a list of featured and peer reviewed publications and of awarded honors. Her CV<ref name=":1" /> includes a more comprehensive list of her activities and publications, including some poetry.

In a personal essay, Karaali has described how teaching an interdisciplinary first-year seminar led her to think about math, writing, and social justice in new ways.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Karaali |first1=Gizem |title=Humanistic Mathematics: An Oxymoron? |journal=Diversity & Democracy |date=Spring 2012 |volume=15 |issue=2 |page=21 |url=https://scholarship.claremont.edu/pomona_fac_pub/167/ |access-date=6 April 2022 |archive-date=7 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210507231458/https://scholarship.claremont.edu/pomona_fac_pub/167/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Karaali and the mathematician [[Lily Khadjavi]] have co-edited two books, ''Mathematics for Social Justice: Resources for the College Classroom'' and ''Mathematics for Social Justice: Focusing on Quantitative Reasoning and Statistics'', which provide resources for mathematics instructors who want to add social justice topics to their courses or create new mathematics courses centered around social justice. The books are published by the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] Press, an imprint of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics for Social Justice: Resources for the College Classroom and Focusing on Quantitative Reasoning and Statistics (2-Volume Set) |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/cdn-1639207548218/clrm-karaali-set/ |website=AMS Bookstore |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=6 April 2022 |archive-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220112174144/https://bookstore.ams.org/cdn-1639207548218/clrm-karaali-set/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Edholm |first1=Christina |title=Mathematics for Social Justice: An Interview with the Editors |journal=MAA Focus |date=June–July 2020 |url=http://digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com/publication/?i=663226&article_id=3695296&view=articleBrowser |access-date=6 April 2022 |archive-date=6 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406222341/http://digitaleditions.walsworthprintgroup.com/publication/?i=663226&article_id=3695296&view=articleBrowser |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2010, Karaali won the Young Investigator Award from the [[National Security Agency]]. She stated that she would use the prize winnings to continue her research on Yang-Baxter equations, super quantum groups, and [[Hopf algebra]]s.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://ccms.claremont.edu/content/Gizem-Karaali-Pomona-receives-Young-Investigator-Award-29756-National-Security-Agency| title=Gizem Karaali (Pomona) receives Young Investigator Award of $29,756 from the National Security Agency| website=Claremont Center for the Mathematical Sciences| access-date=18 March 2019| date=September 2010| archive-date=11 August 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811094859/http://ccms.claremont.edu/content/Gizem-Karaali-Pomona-receives-Young-Investigator-Award-29756-National-Security-Agency| url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Karaali is married to mathematician [[Stephan Ramon Garcia]]. Together they have two children.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4719|title=Stephan Ramon Garcia to Receive Inaugural Dolciani Prize|website=American Mathematical Society|date=26 November 2018|access-date=18 March 2019|archive-date=20 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420011743/http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=4719|url-status=live}}</ref>
